title: Equal-budget coactivity-guided preservation of identified adjacency under input changes
status: Prospectively fixed exploratory follow-up after prior experiments; not a public preregistration
scientific_question: Does selecting less activity-disruptive statistically matched rewiring using one reference input improve closed-loop fidelity under held-out inputs?
family: One existing homogeneous E/I block-random original, seed 99; 125 chunks, 100 synchronized copies per chunk
kernel: Frozen source, canonical explicit routing, same dormant/refractory semantics; no model repair or proxy

budget.definition: Number of original adjacency pairs removed in each arm; all edges retained in rewired graph

candidate_pool.algorithm: Independent from original. Within arm select two unused original rows without replacement, same weight bits/delay; require distinct source/target, no loops or duplicate current pairs, and no new pair in ORIGINAL adjacency. After each accepted target swap mark both rows used. Stop at exact per-arm missing-original-pair budget.
candidate_pool.sampling: Conditional monotone first-legal-swap construction; no uniform random-graph/null/mixing claim

selection.training_activity: inherited/training-original.npz state_bits[:, :, 0]/100, source slots 0..297 inclusive (298 columns), corresponding to recurrent arrival n+2 within 300 slots
selection.weights: Separate excitatory and inhibitory source matrices W^q[target,source]; no E/I cancellation
selection.mean: J_mean = L sum_q ||DeltaW^q mu||_2^2; mu is source temporal mean, L=298
selection.coactivity: J_coactivity = sum_q ||DeltaW^q S||_F^2; uncentered zero-lag second-order coactivity, invariant under a common time permutation; not temporal ordering or a learned memory
selection.shuffled: J_shuffled = mean over 32 independent per-source time permutations of J_coactivity; one shared set of permutations per block for all candidates; preserves each source spike-count distribution, destroys across-source alignment
selection.shuffle_rng: numpy Generator(PCG64), repeat order then source index order, permutation(L)
selection.analytic_shuffle_diagnostic: L sum_q ||DeltaW^q mu||^2 + sum_q,j ||DeltaW^q[:,j]||^2 C_jj, C=(S-mu)(S-mu)^T. Diagnostic only; never selects.
selection.score_scope: Full DeltaW, including interference between simultaneous swaps; no rank truncation; 64 scores per policy except uniform random
selection.overlap: Keep all policy memberships; simulate unique graph bytes once per input; do not replace overlapping selections

heldout_design: 2x2 mask/waveform design with train as one cell; three held-out conditions, not three independent networks. Split input ends at 12 ms rather than 8 ms, shortening post-input observation.

primary.metric: Identified raw-slot spike L1 normalized by same-input original total spike count
primary.aggregation: Within block equal-weight mean of three held-out errors, then paired coactivity minus random; report mean, median, full range and win/tie/loss counts across 10 blocks
primary.zero_reference_spikes: Normalized errors undefined; retain and report, do not replace the input
primary.per_input: All training and individual held-out results must also be reported; no selection of most favorable input
primary.success_interpretation: Training score improvement is selection-induced, not evidence. Consistent closed-loop improvement over random and mean/shuffled is needed to attribute a transfer benefit to across-source coactivity; mixed/negative results retained without protocol revision

secondary: identified cumulative-count L1 and cumulative/raw ratio Rcount (undefined if raw zero)
van Rossum tau=1 ms full exponential tail, representative spikes, normalized by same-input original spike count
absolute and original-channel-standardized RMS of V/gE/gI
spike equality and first differing slot
source edge visits and queue events only as diagnostics, not runtime
statistics: Conditional paired descriptive results across 10 graph-search banks, one original graph and one alternate mask. No p-values or generalization intervals; do not pool held-out inputs or duplicate selectors as independent samples. All conditions and selectors reported.
gates: Design/code/source/events locked before any new simulation
All 640 candidates, scores, selections and hashes locked before any held-out simulation
Original train CSV driver identical to archived counts and all ten state fields
Within-chunk identity and finite fields for all runs
Fresh-directory regenerate, rebuild, rerun all unique selected graphs and compare state payload/count CSV and derived numerical outputs
limitations: No biological calibration or larger-model claim
No inferred necessity of specific individual edges; selection optimizes a complete candidate graph
Graph-search effort and training trajectory storage are offline costs, not savings
No adaptation of masks, budgets, pool size, score, horizon or metric after outcomes
